scope: Standing neo-Gothic exterior of the Santa Capilla basilica in central Caracas, including the three-bay west façade, central spire, northern street elevation and principal nave roofs.
state: named footprint, original terrain and two CC0 exterior controls verified

publishedCandidate.subject: Arturo Michelena’s 1897 Multiplication of the Loaves and Fishes, on canvas inside the church.

archivalCandidate.subject: 1902 published city stereograph. A partial church elevation appears at the edge of frame. The basilica tower and portal were rebuilt in 1917–1921.
archivalCandidate.use: Period context pending confirmation of the photographed church and its relevance to the standing facade.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: Archival study identifies the 1883 north nave, 1889–1892 southern nave and side narthexes, and the 1917–1921 main portal and nave beneath the reinforced central tower.
The conservation survey records alterations for Avenida Urdaneta, replacement of the nave side covers with flat concrete after 1967, and a later color change.
The architecture guide locates the façade opposite Plaza Andrés Eloy Blanco and describes three pointed entrances, the central rose and needle spire.

next: Model the present standing exterior with the distinctive Urdaneta street wall, central tower and documented west portal.
